blocks.text: INNNEWS - Preliminary government Prabowo Subianto EstoGiran Rakaking faces a familiar paradox in Indonesian political history: national popularity is relatively stable, but the region's reconstruction is beginning to increase. From the industrial region, the resource-producing area, to the national economic buffer area, there's a similar sentiment for criticism of the Free Bergizi Eating Program (MBG), transfer cuts to the Area (TKD), and the mistrust that hasn't been fully restored since the Constitution of the Constitution 90 / PUU- XXI / 2023.

MBG is the main symbol of new government ambition. With the budget support of hundreds of trillion rupees, this program has been positioned as the largest human development project in the last decade. Politically, it's effective to maintain public support, especially in young and low-class voters who feel immediate benefits.

But popularity isn't always identical to good management. In the field, there was a problem about the quality of food distribution, the risk of food security, as well as central kitchen dominance that was judged to outrank local UMKM. The main problem is not just technical, it's institutional. The government seems to be building a large-scale national program faster than the readiness of bureaucratic coordination and regional participation.

This phenomenon shows what in the study of policy is called an overstretch policy when the scale of political ambition transcends the capacity of state implementation. The central government is reliant on electrical legitimacy and fiscal power, but it hasn't fully built a stable multiparty management mechanism.

Tensions get more intense when it's associated with fiscal policy. TKD cuts embody perception that the government is moving towards the financial rectorization of the country. Many local governments face dilemmas: on one hand are demanded to maintain local economic growth, on the other side of the fissures room getting narrower.

In the fiscally federalism perspective, this condition creates a vertical fiscally overriding inequality between central income and public service load that remains in the area. The local government still carries the responsibility of education, health, infrastructure and staff shopping, but its budget efficiency is reduced drastically.

It's no surprise that anxiety starts to appear in various industrial areas and resource-producing areas. They feel that their economic contributions to the country are no longer a proportional fissional distribution. When the center enlarges the national project, the area is going through a tagging.

In the midst of that situation, the verdict of Constitution Court number 90 / PUU-XXI / 2023 remains a critical political shadow. It left the impression that state institutions can be influenced by elite interests. As a result, the public no longer assesses policy by its benefits, but also from the legitimacy of the political process behind it.

This pattern shows the trends of top- down developmentalism: countries move very vertically through a major national project, but weak in horizontal coordination with the region. In the short run, models like this can maintain political stability. But in the long run, he risks creating structural resistance when the area feels like it's just a central policy enforcer.

The biggest challenge of Prabowo-Gibran government has not simply maintained a level of public satisfaction, but it's rebuilding the sense of regional ownership of national agenda. Without it, the national strategic program will be accepted as a central project charged to the area.

Therefore, the government needs to move towards the cooperative federalist approach: expand the participation of the region in policy design, repair the TKD formulation based on real needs, and reinforce institutional transparency so that the legitimacy crisis doesn't continue to overshadow new governments.

In the end, national stability is not only defined by the size of a populist program, but by the ability of the state to maintain balance between central power and local confidence. When the area began to feel lost in its position as a partner, the issue was no longer administrative but political.
